kicker: ADVERTISING 2 / CRAFTING FOR A SOCIAL CAUSE
title:
THIS SEAT
HAS A HEAD.
body:
The overlooked second rider.
A campaign on the seat they are about to occupy.

title:
The person
on the second seat.
body:
Cause: pillion helmet use on everyday shared journeys.
Focus: adult driver-pillion pairs, stationary before departure.
Not a new product, app, rental scheme or service.
note: Age 18-30 and private-parking setting are strategic choices, not measured local prevalence.

body:
Passenger fatalities recorded in the non-wearing-of-helmet category in India, 2024.
54,122 total fatalities in that category.
note: MoRTH data via inspected OpenCity table records and Hindustan Times, 12 June 2026. Same underlying dataset; original ministry table cells not directly inspected. Not proof nonuse caused every crash.

title:
Knowing is not
always doing.
body:
346 adult crash patients in one eastern-India hospital sample.
96.6% agreed helmets were essential; 35.7% had used one.
Short-distance travel and forgetfulness were associated with nonuse.
note: Mishra et al., 2025; data March-December 2021. Hospital sample, not national/Mumbai prevalence. Association, not causation. PMC12020946 / DOI 10.4103/ijciis.ijciis_85_24.

title:
Make the second
person present.
body:
Audience: adult student / early-career driver-pillion pairs.
Hypothesis: on an ordinary shared ride, the second seat can become an afterthought.
Put the reminder where the second person is about to sit.
note: Creative hypothesis, not a participant quote. Local reasons for nonuse remain to be tested.

title:
Their own helmet.
Before the ride.
body:
Proposition: the second person needs their own helmet too.
Action: both helmets on; both chinstraps fastened.
Tone: direct, considerate, no blame or simulated enforcement.
note: Correct helmet use reduces risk, not all risk. WHO road-traffic fact sheet, 20 July 2026; PIB helmet guidance, 12 July 2025.

title:
Three routes.
One campaign.
body:
01 SECOND-SEAT MESSAGE - selected: seat is the placement.
02 TWO-PERSON PARKING SLIP - rejected: close receipt precedent.
03 PLUS-ONE RIDE INVITE - reserve: before-ride social message.
note: Receipt precedent: HDFC Bank / STUDDS, The Helmet Receipt, reported February 2026. No claim of exhaustive originality clearance.

title:
The seat supplies
the meaning.
body:
An A6 card rests on the stationary pillion seat.
It addresses the passenger at the mounting decision.
No scan. No sign-up. No new service.
Facilitator removes it before anyone mounts.
note: Opt-in, permissioned, supervised placement only. No adhesive or vehicle alteration. Stop if safe collection cannot be assured.

title:
THIS SEAT
HAS A HEAD.
body:
YOURS.
Pillion passengers need a helmet too.
Put on and fasten your helmet before you ride.
note: Finished A6 artwork supplied as PDF, SVG and PNG. Supervised prototype; remove before mounting.

title:
Where the second
person is about to sit.
body:
A parked vehicle. Engine off. Adult participants opt in.
Message placed briefly on the rear seat.
Card collected and accounted for before mounting.
note: Illustrated placement mockup, not a photograph or evidence of deployment.

title:
Two seats.
Two helmets.
body:
Equal-scale helmet symbols. One clear instruction.
Deep green + warm ivory + signal yellow-green.
Supporting poster reinforces the pre-ride check.
note: No certification marks, police styling, sponsor logo, crash imagery or claim of guaranteed protection.

title:
Who's on your
second seat?
body:
A captioned 15-second illustrated sequence.
One bike / two people / two helmets / both fastened.
Check before the ride, never while riding.
note: HTML motion prototype and vertical artwork supplied. Not live-action footage or a claimed platform deployment.

title:
Small enough
to demonstrate safely.
body:
12 reusable A6 cards + 2 A3 posters.
Permissioned stationary encounter; no unattended placement.
No helmet or vehicle attachments.
No permission? Use the illustrated demonstration only.
note: No partner, venue access, participant consent or filming is claimed to have been secured.

title: INR 700
body:
Cards 180 / Posters 160 / Proofs 160
Consent and tally sheets 50 / Contingency 150
Uses existing print media and a supervised setting.
note: Planning assumptions, not vendor quotes. Excludes labour, travel, permissions, tax changes and helmet purchase.

title:
Did the message
actually arrive?
body:
Proposed comprehension test: 12 consenting adults.
Proposed revision gate: 10 identify passenger helmet use + fastening before departure.
Ask openly about meaning, tone, timing and confusion.
note: No tests conducted. Threshold is an operational design gate, not a validated benchmark. Any safety concern triggers revision.

title:
Measure the check.
Do not promise lives saved.
body:
Optional pilot: aggregate observations of paired departures.
Record both helmets, visible straps and unknown observations.
No plates, faces, names or equipment-certification claims.
An uncontrolled small pilot cannot establish causality.
note: Plan only. Do not report invented lifts, audience quotes, crash reductions or long-term effectiveness.

title:
From evidence
to one clear action.
body:
14 OCT - cause, research / insight, three concepts.
21 OCT - design WIP and feasible comprehension work.
27 OCT - campaign submission.
28 OCT - presentation and final review.
note: Dates as supplied in the assignment brief; brief specifies no year. Actual fieldwork, permissions and outcomes remain unclaimed.

title:
Traceable facts.
Honest limitations.
body:
Mishra et al., 2025 / PMC12020946 / primary hospital study.
MoRTH 2024 data / reproduced OpenCity table + HT reporting.
WHO, Road traffic injuries / updated 20 July 2026.
PIB, Helmet - More Than Just a Shell / 12 July 2025.
MediaNews4u / The Helmet Receipt / 7 February 2026.
note: Complete URLs and claim limits in CAMPAIGN_REPORT and the research ledger. Sources accessed 14 October 2026.

title:
Two seats.
Two helmets.
Both fastened.
body: The second person is not an afterthought.
note: THIS SEAT HAS A HEAD. / STUDENT DESIGN SUBMISSION
